title: Summarizing Quantitative Data: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Summarizing Quantitative Data: Visual Guide

1. Balance Point Drag | a dot plot of 5, 6, 7 and a fourth value you drag from 1 to 100, with the mean marked as a fulcrum and the median as a dashed line | the mean is the balance point and travels with the outlier while the median is a position and barely moves, which is the numeric version of the skew you used to read off a histogram

2. Five Number Box | a box and whisker plot built live from an 11-value data set, with three starting shapes and a slider that pushes the largest value further out | the box spans Q1 to Q3 so its width is the IQR and the line inside it is the median, while whisker asymmetry is what reports skew and the quartiles refuse to move for the tail

3. Squares Not Signs | a deviation table for the population 2, 4, x with a switch between totalling x - mu, |x - mu| and (x - mu)^2 | signed deviations sum to exactly zero for every data set so squaring is what makes a spread measure possible, variance divides the sum of squares by N and the square root restores the original units

4. Why n Minus One | every sample of size n drawn from the population 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 enumerated exactly, averaging the two candidate divisors against the true variance of 8 | dividing by n is biased low at every sample size because the sample mean is fitted to the same data, and n - 1 corrects for estimating the centre rather than for being a sample

5. Tilt The Cloud | a nine-point scatter whose slope, curvature and y-units you control, showing covariance, Pearson r and Spearman rho together | covariance keeps the units of x times y so only its sign is interpretable, Pearson r divides them out and scores linear association only, Spearman scores any monotone pattern, and none of the three is evidence of causation

6. Spread Under Stress | nine response times with a draggable slowest value, crossed with add 5, multiply by 3 and multiply by 0, reporting range, standard deviation, variance, IQR and MAD side by side | adding a constant leaves every spread untouched while multiplying scales them all by the factor and the variance by its square, and the resistance ranking runs range, standard deviation, IQR, MAD
